Websites, business software and AI chatbots, plus the local SEO, Google Maps and ads that bring you customers. Built for Houston small businesses.
Pacific Marketing Solution offers small business marketing and software in Houston from one team: a marketer who has grown small businesses and an engineering lead who has shipped 50+ software platforms. You get one plan, one point of contact and clear numbers every month.

## Running a small business shouldn’t mean chasing every lead yourself
Most owners we talk to feel the same three pressures.

### Customers can’t find you
Competitors show up on Google Maps and in search results while you don’t, so people who are ready to buy call them first.

### Leads slip through the cracks
Calls go to voicemail, website messages wait for days and nobody follows up. Every missed reply is a sale you already paid to attract.

### Your tools don’t talk to each other
Booking, invoicing, a CRM and a website that each work alone mean hours of copying data and no clear view of what is working.

### One team that builds your tools and brings you customers
Most agencies do either the tech or the marketing. We do both, so your website, software and ads are planned and measured together. Everything is delivered online, with Google Meet calls and shared progress updates, whether you are in Katy or Kuala Lumpur.

#### We build
- Websites that load fast and turn visitors into calls
- Business software: booking, CRM, point-of-sale tools and dashboards
- AI chatbots that answer questions and book appointments around the clock

#### We grow
- Local SEO and Google Maps visibility
- Social media content and paid ads on Meta and Google
- Monthly reports on leads, calls and cost per customer

## Questions Houston business owners ask us
Q: How much do marketing and software cost for a small business in Houston?
It depends on scope, and you get a fixed quote in US dollars before any work starts. After the free growth plan call we send a written plan with the price, so there are no surprises.
Q: How soon will I see more calls or bookings?
Ads and chatbots often bring new enquiries within a few weeks, while local SEO usually builds over three to six months. We report calls, leads and bookings every month so you can see the trend.
Q: Can you build custom software like a booking system or CRM?
Yes. Our engineering team builds booking systems, CRMs, point-of-sale tools and dashboards, and connects them to the apps you already use.
Q: Do I have to sign a long-term contract?
No. Projects have a fixed scope, and monthly services can be stopped with notice, so you stay because the work pays off.
Q: Which Houston areas do you serve?
We serve all of Houston and nearby cities, including Katy, Sugar Land, The Woodlands, Pearland, Cypress, Spring and Pasadena. Most of the work happens online, so you never need to drive across town.
Q: Do you work with businesses outside Houston?
Yes. We work with small businesses across the US and in other countries, and everything from planning to reporting happens online.
Q: How do you work with clients in other time zones?
We schedule Google Meet calls at times that suit you and share progress in writing, so you can review updates whenever your day starts. Prices stay in US dollars, and we can quote in other currencies on request.

## Choosing the right services
Q: Which service should a small business start with?
Start with whatever stands between you and your next customer: usually a fast website and a Google Business Profile, then SEO or ads. On the free call we recommend one or two services, not all nineteen.
Q: Can I combine several services in one plan?
Yes. Most clients combine two or three, such as a website, local SEO and a chatbot, and get one plan, one contact and one monthly report.
Q: How much do your services cost?
Each service has a fixed price based on your scope, quoted in US dollars after a free call. Combined plans cost less than buying each service separately.
Q: Do I have to sign a long-term contract?
No. Projects have a fixed scope, and monthly services can be paused or stopped with notice.
Q: Do you only work with businesses in Houston?
No. We are based in Houston and serve the surrounding cities in person, and we work with small businesses across the US and abroad online.
Q: Do you offer services in Spanish?
Yes. We create websites, ads and content in English and Spanish for businesses that serve both audiences.
Q: Who will actually do the work?
Our own team: a marketing lead for strategy, content and ads, and an engineering team for websites, automation and software, with one person as your main contact.

# Never miss a call or a task again: AI agent and voice receptionist development

Our AI agent and voice receptionist development goes beyond a chat box. We build phone agents with Vapi, Retell AI, ElevenLabs and Twilio, multi-agent systems on Claude and OpenAI, and RAG assistants that answer from your own files. For a website or WhatsApp bot only, see AI chatbots.

## Missed calls and manual work cost you every day
These are the problems AI agents are built to remove.

### Calls go to voicemail
After hours, at lunch or when the team is busy, callers hang up and phone the next business.

### Staff repeat the same work
Reading documents, writing summaries and moving data between tools eats whole days.

### Your knowledge is locked in files
Answers sit in PDFs, policies and old emails that nobody has time to search.

### AI agents built, tested and kept under your control
We pick the right model for each job, give every agent clear rules and limits, connect it to your calendar, CRM and phone line, and log every conversation so you can review it. Sensitive data can stay on your own servers. Repetitive hand-offs between tools are handled with n8n and Make automation.

#### What we do
- Map the calls and tasks to hand over
- Build and train the agents on your data
- Connect phone, calendar and CRM
- Test, monitor and improve every week

#### What you get
- Every call answered, day or night
- Hours of manual work taken off your team
- Fast answers from your own documents
- Full logs and code you own

## AI agent services we build
Each agent is designed around one clear job, then connected to the tools you already use.

### Voice AI receptionists
Phone agents on Vapi, Retell AI, ElevenLabs and Twilio that answer, qualify callers and book during the call.
Best for: Clinics, home services, law firms and salons.

### Multi-agent systems
Teams of AI agents on Claude, OpenAI, LangChain and MCP that research, write, check and hand work to each other.
Best for: Businesses with multi-step work.

### RAG knowledge assistants
Assistants that search your documents in a vector database and answer with sources.
Best for: Teams with manuals, policies and case files.

### Private, self-hosted AI
Models run on your own cloud GPUs so client data is never sent to an outside AI company.
Best for: Legal, medical and finance firms.

### AI inside your app
Claude, OpenAI or Gemini features added to your existing software, with prompt controls for your admins.
Best for: SaaS products and internal tools.

### Speech and voice features
Speech-to-text with Whisper, natural AI voices and call summaries sent to your CRM.
Best for: Coaching, wellness and support teams.

## AI agent and voice AI questions, answered
Q: What is the difference between an AI chatbot and an AI agent?
A chatbot answers messages. An AI agent can also take actions: book an appointment, update your CRM, read a document or pass work to another agent.
Q: Can an AI receptionist answer my business phone?
Yes. We connect a voice agent to your number with Twilio, Vapi or Retell AI. It answers, asks your questions, books into your calendar and sends a summary.
Q: Will callers know they are talking to AI?
We recommend the agent says so at the start. Modern voices sound natural, and the agent can transfer to a person at any time.
Q: Is my data safe with AI agents?
We set strict rules on what each agent can see and do, log every action, and can run models on your own servers so client data never leaves your control.
Q: Which AI models and tools do you use?
Claude, OpenAI and Gemini models, LangChain and MCP for agents, Vapi, Retell AI, ElevenLabs and Twilio for voice, and vector databases for document search.
Q: How much does a custom AI agent cost?
It depends on the number of agents, channels and integrations. After a discovery call we send a fixed-scope quote in US dollars, paid in milestones.
Q: Who owns the AI agent when it is finished?
You do. You get the source code, prompts, documentation and access to the cloud accounts it runs on.

## You are spending money without seeing profit
These are the reporting problems we fix most often.

### Numbers live in five tabs
Shopify, Stripe, Meta, Google and a spreadsheet each tell a different story.

### Revenue looks good, profit does not
Without COGS, fees and ad spend in one place, you cannot see what you really keep.

### Reports take hours each week
Someone copies numbers by hand, and decisions wait for the report.

### One source of truth, checked by tests
We connect each data source through its official API, write a tested calculation library for your metrics, and build a simple dashboard your whole team can read. The AI layer turns the numbers into a short summary with the actions worth taking. Store data comes cleanly from Shopify.

- Connect your data sources by API

## Analytics dashboard questions, answered
Q: What is an AI analytics dashboard?
It is a live dashboard that combines data from your store, payments and ad accounts, calculates your key numbers and adds a short AI-written summary of what changed.
Q: Which tools can you connect?
Shopify, Stripe, Meta Ads, Google Ads and most tools with an API, plus your own database or spreadsheets.
Q: What are MER and CAC?
MER is total revenue divided by total ad spend. CAC is what you spend to win one new customer. Together they show if your marketing is paying off.
Q: How do I know the numbers are right?
We write your formulas as a tested calculation library and check them against your own records before launch.
Q: Why not just use Shopify or Google Analytics reports?
Those show one source each. A custom dashboard combines costs, fees and ad spend from every source to show true profit.
Q: How much does a custom dashboard cost?
It depends on the data sources and metrics. After a discovery call we send a fixed-scope quote in US dollars, paid in milestones.
Q: Who owns the dashboard and data?
You do. You get the source code, documentation and access to the cloud accounts it runs on.

## AI search optimization questions, answered
Q: What is AI search optimization?
It is the work of making your business easy for AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews to find, understand and recommend. It is also called answer engine or generative engine optimization.
Q: Can you get my business mentioned in ChatGPT?
We cannot control what ChatGPT says, but we can make your facts clear, consistent and well cited, which makes mentions much more likely. We track the results every month.
Q: Is AI search optimization different from SEO?
It builds on SEO but adds structured facts, direct answers and citations on trusted sites. Most businesses need both.
Q: How long does it take to appear in AI answers?
Fixes to your own site can show up within weeks; broader mentions usually take 2–4 months as AI tools refresh their sources.
Q: How much does AI search optimization cost?
It depends on your site and how much content we create. You get a fixed quote in US dollars after a free audit call.
Q: Do you offer AI search optimization outside Houston?
Yes. AI tools serve users everywhere, so we work with businesses across the US and abroad.
Q: What is llms.txt and do I need one?
llms.txt is a short summary file that helps AI tools understand your site. It is quick to add, and we include it in our setup.

## AI website questions, answered
Q: Can you really launch a website in 3–7 days?
Yes, for sites up to about 6 pages, as long as we get your answers and feedback on time. We agree the launch date on the first call.
Q: Will an AI website look generic?
No. AI only writes the first drafts; a designer shapes the layout to your brand and edits every page before launch.
Q: Are AI-built websites good for SEO?
Yes, if they are built properly: fast pages, clear headings, original copy and schema markup. We set all of these up before launch.
Q: What is the difference between Framer and Webflow?
Framer is quicker for simple, beautiful sites; Webflow is better for larger sites with blogs and content collections. We pick the one that fits your plans.
Q: How much does an AI website cost compared with a custom one?
It usually costs less, because AI saves hours of writing and design. We send a fixed quote after the free call.
Q: Do you build AI websites for businesses outside Houston?
Yes. We work with clients across the US and worldwide, fully online.
Q: Can I move to a custom website later?
Yes. Your content, images and domain move with you when you are ready for a custom build.

## Business automation questions, answered
Q: What can I automate in my small business?
Lead capture, follow-ups, appointment reminders, invoices, payment reminders, reviews and reports are the most common. We find the biggest time savers on the free call.
Q: How much does business automation cost?

Q: Should I use Zapier, Make or n8n?
Zapier is easiest, Make is cheaper for complex flows and n8n is best for heavy or private workloads. We recommend the one that fits your volume and budget.
Q: HubSpot or GoHighLevel: which CRM is better?
HubSpot suits B2B teams that want a polished CRM; GoHighLevel suits local businesses and agencies that want texts, funnels and booking in one place. We set up both.
Q: Will automation replace my staff?
No. It removes repetitive tasks so your team can spend more time with customers.
Q: Do you set up automations for businesses outside Houston?
Yes. We work online with clients across the US and worldwide.
Q: What happens if an automation breaks?
We add error alerts, document every workflow and fix issues quickly on our care plans.

Once or twice a month works for most local businesses, and weekly for active online stores, as long as each email is useful.

Yes, they are usually among the best-earning messages a store sends, because they reach people who were about to buy.

## Paid ads questions, answered
Q: How much does ads management cost for a small business?
Our fee depends on the platforms and number of campaigns, and your ad budget is paid directly to Google, Meta or TikTok. We send a fixed monthly fee in US dollars after a free call.
Q: How much should I spend on ads each month?
Enough to get meaningful data, usually a few hundred US dollars a month per platform for a local business. We will suggest a starting budget based on your goals and margins.
Q: Should I use Facebook ads or Google ads?
Use Google when people already search for what you sell, and Facebook and Instagram to reach people before they search. Many businesses do best with both.
Q: How soon will I get leads from ads?
Most campaigns bring first leads within the first 1–2 weeks, and costs usually improve over the first 4–6 weeks of testing.
Q: Why are my current ads not converting?
Usually it is missing tracking, broad targeting, weak offers or a slow landing page. Our free audit shows which one it is.

Yes. Ads run in your own accounts, and you keep all data and access if you stop working with us.

## SEO questions, answered
Q: How much do SEO services cost for a small business in Houston?
It depends on how competitive your market is and how much content and link building you need. We send a fixed monthly price in US dollars after a free audit call, with no long-term contract.
Q: How long does SEO take to work?
Most sites see early movement in 2–3 months and meaningful lead growth in 4–6 months. Fixing technical problems can show results sooner.
Q: Is SEO better than Google Ads?
SEO builds free traffic that lasts, while ads bring leads immediately but stop when you stop paying. Many businesses use ads now and SEO for the long term.
Q: Can you guarantee first place on Google?
No honest agency can guarantee rankings, because Google decides. We guarantee clear work, monthly reports and a plan focused on leads.
Q: What do you need from me to start SEO?
Access to your website, Google Search Console and Analytics, and 30 minutes to explain your best services and customers.
Q: Do you do SEO for businesses outside Houston?
Yes. We run SEO for businesses across the US and abroad, in English and Spanish.
Q: How will I know SEO is working?
You get a monthly report showing rankings, organic visitors, calls and form leads from search, plus what we did and what comes next.

## Shopify questions, answered
Q: How much does it cost to set up a Shopify store?
It depends on the number of products, the design work and the apps you need. We send a fixed quote in US dollars after a free call; Shopify’s own monthly plan is paid separately to Shopify.
Q: How long does it take to launch a Shopify store?
Most stores launch in 2–4 weeks. Large catalogs and migrations can take a little longer, and we agree the date before we start.
Q: Should I choose Shopify or WooCommerce?
Choose Shopify if you want a store that is simple to run and secure without maintenance; choose WooCommerce if you already have a WordPress site and want full control. We set up both and will recommend the better fit for you.
Q: Can you move my store to Shopify without losing sales?
Yes. We move products, customers and orders, keep your product addresses with redirects and switch over when traffic is low.
Q: Do you work with Houston businesses that also sell in store?
Yes. We connect Shopify POS or your inventory so online and in-store stock stay in sync, and set up local pickup and delivery.
Q: Do you build stores for brands outside Houston?
Yes. We work with brands across the US and in other countries, entirely online.
Q: Can you help me get sales after launch?
Yes. We run Meta and Google shopping ads, email flows and product videos, and report sales every month.

## Website development questions, answered
Q: How much does a small business website cost in Houston?
The price depends on the number of pages, whether we write the copy and the features you need, such as booking or online payments. After a free call we send a fixed quote in US dollars, so the price never changes halfway through.
Q: How long does it take to build a website?
A typical business website takes 3–6 weeks from first call to launch. A single landing page can be live in under a week, and larger sites with custom features take longer.
Q: Should I use Wix or Squarespace or have a custom website built?
Use a template builder if you need something simple and cheap; choose a custom build if you want speed, better rankings and features that bring in leads. We will tell you honestly which fits your budget on the free call.
Q: Will my new website rank on Google?
Yes, it will be built to rank: clean code, fast pages, proper headings, schema markup and a Google Business Profile connection. Ranking for competitive Houston searches also takes ongoing SEO, which we can add.
Q: Can you redesign my site without losing my Google traffic?
Yes. We keep the pages and addresses that already rank, set up redirects for anything that moves and check Search Console after launch.
Q: Do you work with businesses outside Houston?
Yes. We build websites for small businesses across the US and in other countries, with all reviews and approvals done online.
Q: How do we work together if I am in another time zone?
We schedule Google Meet calls at times that suit you and share design previews and progress in writing, so you can review them whenever your day starts.

<!-- https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/glossary/ -->
Page title: Marketing Terms Explained | Pacific Marketing Solution
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/glossary/
Summary: Plain-English meanings of common marketing words such as SEO, AEO, GEO, CRM, CTR, CPC, conversion, funnel and white-label.

# Marketing terms explained in plain English.
Short, simple meanings for the words you will hear when you work with a marketing team.

## Finding you online

### SEO (Search Engine Optimization)
The work of helping your website appear higher in search results such as Google, so more people find you without paying for ads.

### AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)
Writing and organising your content so search tools can pick it as the direct answer to a question, for example in a featured snippet or a voice assistant reply.

### GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)
Making your business easy for AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity to find, understand and mention when people ask them questions.

### Keyword
A word or phrase people type into a search box, such as "dent repair near me".

### Indexing
When a search engine adds your page to its list of pages it can show. A page that is not indexed cannot appear in search results.

### Organic traffic
Visitors who find your website through unpaid search results.

### Structured data (schema)
Hidden labels in a web page that tell search engines and AI tools what the page is about, such as a business address or a list of questions and answers.

## Reading the numbers

### Impression
One time your page or ad is shown to someone.

### Click-through rate (CTR)
The share of people who clicked after seeing your page or ad. If 100 people see it and 3 click, the click-through rate is 3%.

### Average position
Where your page typically appears in search results. Position 1 is the top, and positions 11 to 20 are usually on the second page.

### Conversion
A valuable action a visitor takes, such as sending a form, calling you or booking a meeting.

### Conversion rate
The share of visitors who convert. If 200 people visit and 10 send a form, the conversion rate is 5%.

## Advertising

### Cost per click (CPC)
What you pay each time someone clicks your ad.

### Cost per conversion
Your total ad spend divided by the number of conversions. It tells you what each enquiry or sale costs you.

### Landing page
The page a person arrives on after clicking an ad or link, built to get them to take one action.

### Funnel
The steps a person goes through from first seeing your business to becoming a customer.

### Performance marketing
Paid advertising that is measured by results, such as leads or sales, instead of views.

## Tools and ways of working

### CRM (Customer Relationship Management)
Software that keeps your customers, enquiries and follow-ups in one place so nothing is forgotten.

### Automation
Setting software to do routine tasks for you, such as sending a reply or reminding you to follow up.

### AI assistant or chatbot
A program that answers questions in everyday language, on a website, in WhatsApp or on the phone.

### White-label
Work done by one company and delivered under another company's brand name.
Related services: SEO, AEO & GEO Performance marketing and funnels AI automation and CRM White-label services

## Ready to talk it through?
Tell us what you are trying to achieve and we will suggest where to begin.

<!-- https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/a-low-cost-per-click-needs-conversion-tracking/ -->
Page title: Low Cost Per Click: Why Conversion Tracking Matters
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/a-low-cost-per-click-needs-conversion-tracking/
Summary: A $0.78 click sounds cheap, but is it working? Learn why cost per click needs conversion tracking, using a real Google Ads campaign.

# A $0.78 click is only good news if you can see what happens next
Allen Jacobi Law's campaign delivered 717 clicks for $558. Why cost per click alone cannot judge it.
2 min read · Based on: Allen Jacobi Law, Naples Dent Away

## At a glance
Allen Jacobi Law's campaign was shown 24.3K times and earned 717 clicks, a click-through rate of about 3% (calculated), at an average of $0.78 per click. For $558 in total, that is efficient outreach and targeted visibility.

## Do not compare cost per click across businesses
In another campaign we ran for a dent repair service, the average click cost about $2.89, almost four times as much. The two businesses sell different services in different markets, so the click prices are not comparable. What counts is the cost of a qualified enquiry.

## What the dashboard did not show
The figures supplied for this campaign cover clicks and spend. They do not include how many visitors contacted the firm. A cheap click that never becomes an enquiry is still wasted money, and an expensive click that becomes a client can be a bargain.

## Setting up the full picture
- Record contact forms, calls and booking requests as conversions in Google Ads.
- Add call tracking if most enquiries come by phone.
- Ask each new enquiry how they found the firm.
- Report cost per qualified enquiry next to cost per click.
Figures come from the Google Ads dashboard screenshots supplied with the project. Calculated figures are marked.

Page title: Meta Ads Objectives: Clicks or Conversations?
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/clicks-or-conversations-meta-ads-objective/
Summary: How to choose between link clicks and messaging conversations on Meta Ads, with real costs from three industrial-products campaigns.

# Clicks or conversations? Choosing the right Meta Ads objective
Shahid Enterprizes ran three campaigns with different goals, and their numbers cannot be compared directly.
2 min read · Based on: Shahid Enterprizes

## At a glance

### Mega Flecks Industrial Belt
conversations
per conversation
≈ USD 0.080
spend
≈ USD 5.41

### Agro Power Belts (WhatsApp)
link clicks
2,813
per click
≈ USD 0.0024
≈ USD 6.76

### Agro Power Belts (Harvester)
≈ USD 0.109
≈ USD 9.03
Shahid Enterprizes sells industrial belts, where buyers usually want to talk before they buy. We ran three Meta campaigns, and two of them were built to start messaging conversations.

## Different goals, different numbers
The two conversation campaigns produced 68 and 83 conversations, 151 in total, at ≈ USD 0.080 and ≈ USD 0.109 each. The third was a WhatsApp link campaign built for clicks: 2,813 clicks at ≈ USD 0.0024 each. A cost of ≈ USD 0.0024 per click and a cost of ≈ USD 0.079 per conversation measure different things, so putting them in one chart would mislead.

## What the two conversation campaigns show
The Harvester campaign cost about 37% more per conversation than the Mega Flecks campaign (calculated). Across both, the blended cost was about USD 0.096 per conversation (calculated). The cause could be the audience, the product or the creative, and the report does not say which.

## How to choose an objective
- Pick the one result that matters most for each campaign.
- Use a conversation objective when buyers want to ask questions first.
- Use link clicks when you want people on a page, then track what they do there.
- Report every campaign against its own goal.

## What we would do next
- Track how many conversations become quote requests and sales.
- Compare the creative used in the two conversation campaigns.
- Reply quickly: a conversation only has value if someone answers.
Figures come from the live Meta Ads dashboard screenshot supplied with the project. Calculated figures are marked.
Amounts are shown in US dollars, converted from the ad account’s local currency at about 277 to 1 (October 2026), so they are approximate.

<!-- https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/fix-indexing-before-writing-more-content/ -->
Page title: Fix Website Indexing First: A Law Firm SEO Case
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/fix-indexing-before-writing-more-content/
Summary: Why search engines must index your pages before new content helps, and how fixing indexing for a law firm led to qualified leads by month three.

# Fix indexing first: how the SEO for Allen Jacobi Law began
A strong reputation does not help if search engines cannot index the site. What we fixed first and what followed.
2 min read · Based on: Allen Jacobi Law, Our Village

## At a glance
Allen Jacobi Law is an entertainment law firm with a strong reputation, but its website had indexing issues. Pages that are not indexed cannot appear in search results, so no amount of new content would have helped until that was fixed.

## The order of the work
- Resolve the indexing problems so the right pages could be found and listed.
- Optimise the existing content for the searches clients use.
- Add more long-tail keywords: longer, more specific phrases that match what people really type.
Traffic picked up within a month. By the third month, qualified leads were coming in through organic search.

## Why the order matters
It is tempting to start by writing. But new content on pages that search engines cannot index is wasted effort. Checking indexing first tells you whether the problem is the pages themselves or simply that they are not being found.

## Causes we check
- Pages blocked by robots rules or marked noindex by mistake.
- Duplicate pages or wrong canonical tags.
- Thin or near-empty pages.
- A missing or outdated sitemap.
- Server errors and broken redirects.
These are typical causes, not a description of every site.
Our Village, a parenting services app, had a similar starting point: a good product with poor online visibility. After optimising the website and targeting the right keywords, traffic grew significantly and users started finding the app through organic search.

## What we would do next
- Keep watching the coverage report for new indexing issues.
- Turn the long-tail searches that work into dedicated pages.
- Measure enquiries, not just visits.
Details come from the project notes and the Google Search Console screenshot supplied with the project.

# 155,000 link clicks: what three Meta campaigns show about cost per click
Primax Solar Energy's campaigns cost ≈ USD 0.0059 to USD 0.0070 per click, and the biggest campaign was the most expensive.
2 min read · Based on: Primax Solar Energy

## At a glance

### Luxeed Lithium Battery
link clicks
16,030
per click
≈ USD 0.0059

### Galaxy Dual
83,239
≈ USD 0.0070

### Nexa Series
55,899
≈ USD 0.0064
Primax Solar Energy ran three campaigns that together produced 155,168 link clicks.

## The biggest campaign cost the most per click
Galaxy Dual delivered about 54% of all the clicks (83,239) at ≈ USD 0.0070 per click. Luxeed was the cheapest at ≈ USD 0.0059. The gap is around 20% (calculated). A common reason is that as a campaign reaches more people, it moves beyond its cheapest audiences. We do not have the audience data to say whether that happened here.

## A blended figure
Weighting each campaign by its clicks gives a blended cost of about USD 0.0067 per click and a total spend of roughly USD 1,040. Both are calculated from the figures above.

## Traffic is not sales
A link click shows interest, not a purchase. A solar business needs enquiries and quotes, so clicks are the first number to check, not the last.

## What we would do next
- Measure what each campaign produces: quote requests, calls and WhatsApp messages.
- Compare cost per enquiry, not only cost per click.
- Test narrower audiences on the largest campaign.
- Look at why Luxeed's clicks were cheaper and whether that applies to the others.

<!-- https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/reading-a-google-ads-report-beyond-clicks/ -->
Page title: How to Read a Google Ads Report: Clicks to Conversions
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/reading-a-google-ads-report-beyond-clicks/
Summary: Follow a $1,720 Google Ads campaign from impressions to cost per conversion, and learn why clicks alone do not show whether ads are working.

# Clicks are not results: reading a Google Ads report from click to conversion
A $1,720 campaign for Naples Dent Away, followed step by step from impressions to cost per conversion.
2 min read · Based on: Naples Dent Away

## At a glance
Naples Dent Away, a dent repair service in Naples, Florida, ran a Google Ads campaign to raise its online visibility. Here is how we read the report.

## Step 1: did people see and click the ads?
The ads were shown 25,000 times and got 595 clicks, a click-through rate of about 2.4% (calculated). The click-through rate was strong, so the ads and keywords were reaching the right people.

## Step 2: what did a click cost?
With $1,720 spent across 595 clicks, the average cost per click was about $2.89.

## Step 3: how many clicks became enquiries?
Nine conversions from 595 clicks is a conversion rate of about 1.5% (calculated), or roughly $191 per conversion (calculated). This is the number that decides whether a campaign pays for itself.

## What the report points to
Strong clicks but few conversions means the weak spot is after the click: the landing page, the offer, or how easily a visitor can get in touch. That is why the report named conversion rate optimisation as the clear next area.
Illustration only, not a result: if the same 595 clicks converted at 3% instead of 1.5%, the campaign would produce about 18 conversions and the cost per conversion would fall to about $96. Improving the page can matter more than buying more clicks.

## What we would do next
- Check the landing page on a phone: speed, a call button and a clear next step.
- Track calls and form submissions as conversions.
- Send each ad group to a page that matches the search.
- Review search terms and add negative keywords.
Figures come from the Google Ads dashboard screenshots supplied with the project. Calculated figures are marked.

## Keep reading.

### A $0.78 click is only good news if you can see what happens next

<!-- https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/three-seo-reports-side-by-side/ -->
Page title: How to Read an SEO Report: CTR vs Average Position
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/three-seo-reports-side-by-side/
Summary: See how three real SEO projects compare on clicks, impressions, click-through rate and average position, and what each number does and does not tell you.

# Three SEO reports side by side: what the numbers show and what they hide
Skin Body Health, Allen Jacobi Law and Pure Hope Weight Loss share a pattern, and an average position that hides a lot.
2 min read · Based on: Skin Body Health, Allen Jacobi Law, Pure Hope Weight Loss
Search Console reports are easy to read as a score: more clicks is good, fewer is bad. Put three of our SEO projects next to each other and the picture gets more interesting.

## At a glance

### Skin Body Health
clicks
216
impressions
7.3K
average CTR
average position
17.5

### Allen Jacobi Law
471
9.85K
4.8%

### Pure Hope Weight Loss
201
3.83K
5.2%
24.5

## 1. The same average position can give different click-through rates
Skin Body Health and Allen Jacobi Law both averaged position 17.5, which is usually the second page of results. One earned a 3% click-through rate and the other 4.8%. Position decides whether people can see you. The title, the description and how closely the page matches the search decide whether they click.

## 2. A lower average position can still come with a high click-through rate
Pure Hope Weight Loss has the lowest average position of the three (24.5) and the highest click-through rate (5.2%). Average position blends every search the site appears for. A handful of well-matched searches ranking near the top can lift the click-through rate while many others sit far down the results. The report we were given does not break this down, so we treat it as a question to investigate, not a conclusion.

## 3. Impressions set the ceiling
Allen Jacobi Law had the most impressions (9.85K) and the most clicks (471). Pure Hope had the fewest impressions (3.83K) and the fewest clicks (201). Clicks follow impressions, so growth means appearing for more of the searches your customers really use. In the Allen Jacobi Law and Pure Hope projects that included adding long-tail keywords, the longer and more specific phrases people type. Skin Body Health started with targeted keywords and fresh content.

## What we would do next with these reports
- Open the query-level report and see which searches produce the clicks.
- Rewrite titles and descriptions on pages with many impressions but few clicks.
- Strengthen pages sitting between positions 11 and 30 with better content and internal links.
- Track enquiries from search, not only clicks.
Figures come from the Google Search Console screenshots supplied with each project.

<!-- https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/voice-ai-agents-three-builds/ -->
Page title: Voice AI Agents in Practice: Three Builds
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/voice-ai-agents-three-builds/
Summary: A voice coaching platform, an AI phone receptionist and lead re-engagement calls: what our voice agent builds share, and what to plan first.

# Voice AI agents in practice: three builds and what they share
A coaching platform, a phone receptionist and lead re-engagement calls. What our AI engineer's voice agent projects have in common.
2 min read · Based on: Our AI engineer's Upwork portfolio

## At a glance
- 5 specialist voice coaches behind one manager agent
- 1 call to answer and book an appointment
- 243 automated tests on the Airtime Media agents
Voice agents are among the AI builds businesses ask us about most. Here are three that our AI engineer, Nauman N., has shipped, and the patterns they share.

## The three builds
- Voice coaching platform (FastAPI, React, ElevenLabs, Claude): a manager agent routes each user to one of 5 specialist voice coaches.
- AI phone receptionist (Twilio, FastAPI, Next.js, Claude): answers calls and books appointments during the call.
- Airtime Media voice agents (Twilio, Python): re-engage leads on inbound and outbound calls.

## 1. One job per agent
The coaching platform does not ask one agent to do everything. A manager agent decides which coach the user should talk to, and each of the five coaches covers one area. Smaller jobs are easier to test and to improve one at a time.

## 2. Every call should end in an action
The receptionist does more than answer questions: it books the appointment while the caller is still on the line. The lead re-engagement agents work the same way. The aim of each call is a next step, not just a conversation.

## 3. Automated tests before launch
Phone calls are slow to check by hand, so these builds lean on automated tests. The Airtime Media project is covered by 243 of them.

## Before you build a voice agent
- Write down the one action each call should end with, such as a booking.
- List the systems the agent must read from or write to, such as your calendar or CRM.
- Decide when a call should be handed to a person.
- Plan how you will test it before real customers call.
Based on our AI engineer's Upwork portfolio and project notes. See the full project list on our Work page.

---

<!-- https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/tech-stack-behind-our-ai-and-saas-builds/ -->
Page title: The Tech Stack Behind Our AI and SaaS Builds
Address: https://pacificmarketingsolution.com/insights/tech-stack-behind-our-ai-and-saas-builds/
Summary: The tools we use to build AI agents, voice agents and SaaS products, from Next.js and FastAPI to Claude, LangGraph, RAG and n8n.

# The tech stack behind our AI and SaaS builds
What we build AI agents, voice agents and SaaS products with, and why each part is there.
2 min read · Based on: Our AI engineer's Upwork profile and portfolio

## At a glance
- 9+ years building software
- 50+ platforms shipped
- 33 projects in his Upwork portfolio
Clients often ask what we build with. This is the stack our AI engineer, Nauman N., uses across the AI and SaaS projects on our Work page, grouped by the job each part does.

## The app people use
Next.js, React and TypeScript for the web app, with FastAPI (Python) or Node.js behind it. PostgreSQL or Supabase store the data. Stripe handles payments and subscriptions, as in the pet care booking marketplace and the custom GPT community platform.

## The AI layer
The Claude API and the OpenAI API handle language tasks, with LangChain and LangGraph running the agents. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a vector database lets an AI answer from your own documents. In the legal research platform it runs on a self-hosted model, so client documents never reach a third-party API. MCP gives agents a standard way to use tools.

## Voice
ElevenLabs, Vapi, Retell AI and Twilio power voice agents and phone calls, such as the AI phone receptionist that books appointments during the call.

## Automation and CRM
n8n, Make and Zapier connect apps. GoHighLevel, HubSpot and Airtable hold leads and customer records. The Shipbling project, for example, uses n8n workflows to automate a Shopify store.

## Hosting and quality
Docker and AWS for hosting, with automated tests on the larger builds: 93 on the OrbitOS profit dashboard and 243 on the Airtime Media voice agents.

## What we look at when choosing
- The tools your team already uses.
- Keeping your data in systems you own.
- The simplest setup that does the job, with agents only where they save real work.
Based on our AI engineer's Upwork profile and portfolio, October 2026.
